Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:10:1.hebrew: רישא אין רשות משנה - בתיובתא מייתי לה: אמאי קתני רישא, כשהועד בבית בעלים והזיק בבית שואל, חייב באותה נגיחה נזק שלם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:10:1.english: The first clause [indicates that] custody does not change [its status] - [The Gemara] brings this as a refutation: why does the first clause teach [that] when it was rendered forewarned in the owner's house and it caused damage in the borrower's house, he is liable for that goring [to pay] full damages?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:11:1.hebrew: תברא - קשיא אהדדי, ומי ששנה זו לא שנה זו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:11:1.english: Tavra [disjointed] - [The clauses] contradict each other, and [the tanna] who taught this did not teach that.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:12:1.hebrew: לאו כל כמינך כו' - לא שלך היה, ולא נזהרת בשמירתו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:12:1.english: It is not in your power, etc. - It was not yours, and you were not careful in guarding it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:13:1.hebrew: רישא נמי רשות משנה - כלומר, חד תנא הוא, ולתנא דרישא ס"ל נמי הך דסיפא, דרשות משנה. ורישא, משום הכי הרי הוא בחזקתו, שאין כאן שינוי רשות, שכל מקום שהולך שם בעליו עליו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:13:1.english: The first clause also [holds that] custody changes [its status] - That is to say, it is one Tanna, and the Tanna of the first clause also holds this [ruling] of the last clause, that [a change of] custody changes [its status]. And [in] the first clause, for this reason it remains in its [prior] status, for there is no change of custody here, since wherever it goes, the name of its owner is upon it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:14:1.hebrew: מהו לגבי מזבח - שגבי נוגח ברצון והמית אדם, פשיטא לן דפסול כדלקמן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:14:1.english: What is [the law] with regard to the altar - For regarding [an ox] that gores willingly and killed a person, it is obvious to us that it is disqualified, as [stated] below.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:16:1.english: From the cattle - From some of the cattle, and not all of them.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:16:2.hebrew: להוציא רובע ונרבע - ע"פ עד אחד או ע"פ הבעלים, שלא נסקל, דפסול לגבי מזבח:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:16:2.english: To exclude [an animal that] engaged in bestiality and [one that] was the object of bestiality - [That is, where it is known] according to [the testimony of] one witness or according to [the admission of] the owner, so that it was not stoned, [teaching] that it is disqualified for the altar.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:16:3.hebrew: את הנעבד - שעשאו ע"ז והשתחוה לו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:16:3.english: The worshipped [animal] - That [one] made it an object of idol worship and bowed down to it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:16:4.english: The set-aside [animal] - [One] that they designated to sacrifice to idolatry.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:16:5.hebrew: הנוגח - שהמית את האדם ע"פ עד אחד או ע"פ בעלים, ונפטר מן הסקילה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:16:5.english: That gores - [An animal] that killed a person by [the testimony of] a single witness or by [the admission of] the owner, and was [therefore] exempt from stoning.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:17:1.english: If [an animal that] engaged in bestiality is stated, why is [an animal that] gores stated - Behold, both of them are equal in transgression with respect to stoning where there are witnesses.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:19:1.english: [With regard to an animal that] gores, [the Torah] did not render compulsion like willful action - For it is written, "When [an ox] gores," and not when [others] cause it to gore.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:19:2.hebrew: רובע עשה בו אונס כרצון - דנרבע אנוס הוא ונסקל כרובע, דכתיב: "ואת הבהמה תהרוגו":
Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:19:2.english: [With regard to an animal that] engages in bestiality, [the Torah] renders compulsion like [acting] willfully - For [an animal] that is subjected to bestiality is forced, yet it is stoned like [an animal] that engages in bestiality, as it is written: "And you shall kill the beast."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:1:1.hebrew: הוה מודינא ומפטרינא - דפלגא נזקא קנסא, ומודה בקנס פטור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:1:1.english: I would have admitted [liability] and been exempt - For half-damages are a fine, and one who admits to a fine is exempt.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:20:1.english: [Is it] not with regard to an offering? - [Meaning] that it is speaking with regard to an offering.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:21:1.hebrew: לא לקטלא - ולהכי קאמר נוגח לא עשה בו אונס כרצון, לענין סקילה במקום עדים. הלכך, אי לא מעטיה קרא לענין קרבן, לא נפקא לן מרובע אפילו כי עבד ברצון דלפסול, דהא קל הוא מרובע לענין קטלא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:21:1.english: No, [it is] with regard to death - And this is why [the baraita] states, "[With regard to] an animal that gores, [the Torah] did not treat an act under compulsion like a willful act" — with regard to stoning in the presence of witnesses. Therefore, had the verse not excluded it with regard to an offering, we would not have derived from [the case of] an animal that engaged in bestiality that it is disqualified even when it acted willfully, since it is more lenient than an animal that engaged in bestiality with regard to being put to death.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:22:1.hebrew: לא עשה - משמע לא עשה בו הכתוב אונס כרצון, ומהיכא נפקא ליה דפשיטא ליה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 40b:22:1.english: Did not render - [This] implies [that] Scripture did not render compulsion like willingness with respect to it; and from where does [the Tanna] derive it, that it is obvious to him?

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 40b:16:1.hebrew: מן הבהמה להוציא הרובע כו' - בתמורה בפ' כל האסורין (תמורה דף כח: ושם) מפרש דגבי רביעה כתיב בהמה: "ואיש אשר יתן שכבתו בבהמה"; וגבי נעבד כתיב לשון בקר, כדכתיב: "וימירו את כבודם בתבנית שור". ומוקי לה התם ע"פ עד אחד או על פי בעלים, דאי איכא עדים — בני קטלא נינהו. והך ברייתא פליגא אתנא דבי רבי ישמעאל, דנפקא ליה בפרק אין מעמידין (ע"ז דף כג:) מ"כי משחתם בהם מום" כו': "כל מקום שנאמר השחתה אינו אלא דבר ערוה וע"ז". וכן איתא בתמורה (דף כח:) דפליגי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 40b:16:1.english: "From the cattle" — to exclude [an animal that] engaged in bestiality, etc. - In Temurah, in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaAsurin (Temurah 28b ff.), [the Gemara] explains that with regard to bestiality, "behemah" (cattle/beast) is written: "And a man who lies with a beast (behemah)"; and with regard to a worshipped [animal], an expression of "herd" (bakar) is written, as it is written: "And they exchanged their glory for the likeness of an ox." And [the Gemara] there establishes it [as referring to a case proved] by [the testimony of] a single witness or by the owner's [admission], for if there were [two] witnesses, they [the animals] would be subject to execution. And this baraita disagrees with the Tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael, who derives it in the chapter [entitled] Ein Ma'amidin (Avodah Zarah 23b) from "For their corruption is in them, a blemish [is in them]," etc.: "Wherever 'corruption' (hashchatah) is stated, it refers only to sexual immorality and idolatry." And so it is stated in Temurah (28b) that they disagree.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 40b:17:1.hebrew: למה נאמר נוגח - הא דלא קאמר "למה נאמר נעבד" — דההוא פשיטא, דקיל מכולהו, דלאו בר קטלא הוא ובעי קרא יתירא:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 40b:17:1.english: Why is [an animal that] gores stated - [The reason] that he does not say, "Why is [an animal that was] worshipped stated?" is because that [case] is obvious, as it is more lenient than all of them, since it is not liable to the death penalty, and [therefore] requires an extra verse.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 40b:18:1.hebrew: ויש בנוגח כו' - בחד מנייהו סגי, דכיון דלא מפרשי קראי בהדיא הוה אוקימנא ליה בדדמי, ולא שייך למימר "שקולים הם ויבואו שניהם", דהני חומרות אין שקולות, ולא משכחת שיקול אלא בריש מכילתין:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 40b:18:1.english: And there is [a stringency] pertaining to one that gores, etc. - One of them would suffice, for since the verses do not specify [them] explicitly, we would have established it as applying to whatever is similar [to it]. And it is not applicable to say, "They are equal, so let both of them come," because these stringencies are not equal, and you do not find [the principle of] equivalence (shikul) except at the beginning of our tractate.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 40b:19:1.hebrew: רובע עשה בו אונס כרצון - וא"ת: רובע באונס היכי משכחת לה? הא אין קישוי אלא לדעת. וי"ל: כגון שנתקשה למינו, ותקפתו והביאתו עליה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 40b:19:1.english: [With regard to an animal that] engaged in bestiality, [the Torah] renders [a case of] circumstances beyond its control like [a case where it acted] willfully - And if you ask: How can you find [a case of] an animal engaging in bestiality under compulsion, for there is no erection except with intent? One can say [that it is] a case such as where it became aroused for its own species, and [a woman] seized it and brought it upon herself.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 40b:1:1.hebrew: אי תם הוה מודינא ומפטרינא - הך פירכא ליתא למ"ד מודה בקנס ואח"כ באו עדים חייב. וכי קאמר "אפילו למ"ד פלגא נזקא ממונא", ה"ה דהו"מ למפרך: אפילו למ"ד פלגא נזקא קנסא, ולמ"ד מודה בקנס ואח"כ באו עדים חייב, לימא ליה "אי תם הוה מעריקנא ליה לאגמא", אלא חדא מינייהו נקט. וא"ת: והאיך יכול לטעון "אי תם הוה מודינא", "אי תם הוה מעירקנא ליה"? הא קמן שלא הודה ולא הבריח אע"פ שהיה סבור שהיה תם! וי"ל: דמיד אחר נגיחה הוגד לו שהוא מועד. וא"ת: לישני כגון שיש עדים שלא הוגד לו משעת נגיחה עד שיצא לב"ד, ואפ"ה לא הודה ולא הבריח? הא לא שכיח, ועדיפא מיניה קמשני — דקדם ב"ד ותפסוה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 40b:1:1.english: If [the ox] was innocuous, I would have admitted [my liability] and would have been exempt - This difficulty does not apply according to the one who says [that] one who admits to a fine and afterward witnesses come is liable. And when [the Gemara] says "Even according to the one who says [that] half the damage is monetary restitution," the same applies that it could have asked: "Even according to the one who says [that] half the damage is a fine, and according to the one who says [that] one who admits to a fine and afterward witnesses come is liable, let [the borrower] say to him: If it was innocuous, I would have smuggled it out to the marsh" — rather, it mentioned [only] one of them. And if you ask: How can [the borrower] claim "If it was innocuous, I would have admitted" [or] "If it was innocuous, I would have smuggled it out"? Behold, before us [we see] that he neither admitted nor smuggled [it] out, even though he thought that it was innocuous! And one can answer that immediately after the goring he was told that it was forewarned. And if you ask: Let [the Gemara] answer [that we are dealing with a case] where there are witnesses that he was not told from the time of the goring until he came out to court, and even so he neither admitted nor smuggled [it] out? That is uncommon, and [the Gemara] answers a better [answer] than that — that the court seized it first.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 40b:20:1.hebrew: לאו לקרבן - והשתא ה"ק: "נוגח לא עשה בו אונס כרצון", כלומר: השתא נמי שנכתב, אין שייך להעמיד פסול קרבן שלו אלא ברצון, כענין שיש בו חיוב מיתה; הלכך כשלא היה כתוב כלל, אין שייך ללמוד אפילו רצון שלו מרובע, כיון דלא אפשר למילף בכל ענין — בין באונס בין ברצון. וא"ת: אמאי ס"ד דלקרבן קאמר, דפי' דחוק הוא כדמוכח בשמעתין, ומה קשה ליה אי לקטלא קאמר, דשייך שפיר לעשות קולא או חומרא פירכא מקטלא אקרבן כמו שעשה ק"ו מכופר אקרבן? וי"ל: כיון דלא מפרש בהדיא לענין מה עשה ולא עשה אונס כרצון, משמע דלענין קרבן דאיירי ביה קרא קאמר; דאי לענין קטלא, הוה ליה למימר "לא חייב בו אונס כרצון":
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 40b:20:1.english: Is it not with regard to an offering - And now [according to the Gemara's assumption], this is what [the baraita] is saying: "With regard to an animal that gores, [the Torah] does not render circumstances beyond its control like willful action" — that is to say, even now that [an animal that gores] is written [in the Torah], it is only relevant to establish its disqualification from an offering in a case of willful action, similar to a case where there is liability for the death penalty; therefore, when it was not written at all, it would not be appropriate to derive even its willful case from an animal that engaged in bestiality, since it is impossible to derive it in every case — both in circumstances beyond its control and in willful action. And if you ask: Why did it enter [the Gemara's] mind that [the baraita] is speaking with regard to an offering, for it is a forced explanation as is evident in our sugya, and what difficulty would [the Gemara] have if it is speaking with regard to death, since it is completely appropriate to make a leniency or a stringency a refutation from [the law of] death to [the law of] an offering, just as [the baraita] made an a fortiori inference from [the law of] ransom to [the law of] an offering? One can answer: Since [the baraita] does not state explicitly with regard to what it did or did not render circumstances beyond its control like willful action, it implies that it is speaking with regard to an offering, which the verse is discussing; for if it were with regard to death, it should have said "it did not obligate it in circumstances beyond its control as in willful action."

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 40b:2:1.hebrew: הוה מעריקנא ליה לאגמא - תימה, מה טענה היא זו? א"כ היה עושה שלא כדין. ובשלמא לרבי ישמעאל, דאמר ב"ח נינהו, ניחא קצת, דאיכא למימר דהוה אכלנא ליה התם או מזבנינא ליה, ולא הוה אלא כמזיק שעבודו של חבירו, ופטור; אבל לר"ע, דאמר שותפין נינהו, אי הוה מעריק, היה גוזל לו שורו לניזק. ועוד, דב"ד ינדוהו אם לא ישלם, אם יש לו. ונ"ל שרוצה לומר: מתוך דברים אלו שהייתי עושה, היה ניזק מתפשר עמי בדבר מועט והיה מוחל לי, ונמצא שהפסדתני כל היתרון:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 40b:2:1.english: I would have smuggled it out to the marsh - This is astonishing: what kind of claim is this? If so, he would have been acting unlawfully. Now, granted, according to Rabbi Yishmael, who says they are [in a] creditor[-debtor relationship], it is somewhat understandable, for one could say, "I would have eaten it there or sold it," and he would only be like one who damages his fellow's lien, and is exempt; but according to Rabbi Akiva, who says they are partners [in the ox], if he had smuggled [it] out, he would be stealing the injured party's ox from him. Furthermore, the court would place him under a ban if he did not pay, if he has [the means to pay]. And it appears to me that [the Gemara] means to say: Through these things that I would have done, the injured party would have compromised with me for a small amount and forgiven me [the rest], and thus it turns out that you caused me to lose all the excess:

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 40b:4:1.hebrew: אי הכי בעלים אמאי משלמין ח"נ לימא ליה אתפסתיה לתוראי כו' - וא"ת: והרי הוא לא התפיסו בידים, דהא קדים ב"ד ותפסוה, והוא לא היה יודע שהוא מועד? וי"ל: דמיד כשנגח היה לו לחוש יותר שמא היה מועד; דנהי דקודם נגיחה אין לו לחוש כ"כ לפי שאין הפסד מזומן, דשמא לא יגח — אבל לאחר שנגח, מזומנין ב"ד לתופסו, והיה לו לחוש להזהר שלא יפול ביד בית דין:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 40b:4:1.english: "If so, why does the owner pay half the damage? Let him say to him: You let my ox be seized, etc." - And if you ask: Behold, he [the borrower] did not hand it over with his own hands, for the court came first and seized it, and he did not know that it was a mu'ad [a forewarned ox]? And one can answer: Immediately when it gored, he should have been more concerned that perhaps it was a mu'ad; for although before [any] goring he does not need to be so concerned, since there is no imminent loss, as perhaps it will not gore — nevertheless, after it gored, the court is ready to seize it, and he should have been concerned to take care that it not fall into the hands of the court.
